headline: Data Centers Pay Own Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure for large energy users, like data centers, from residential ratepayers to the corporations themselves, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Dominion Energy, Appalachian Voices, consumer and environmental advocates, Governor Abigail Spanberger (with some amendments), Senator Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling.
opponents: Data Center Coalition (initially concerned about language).
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill, HB 1393, seeks to shift energy costs for grid infrastructure, including capacity auctions and distribution infrastructure, onto large energy users like data centers, rather than residential customers. This move is supported by some lawmakers and Dominion Energy, who believe it will lower residential bills and expand energy assistance programs, though the Governor made some amendments.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding their water consumption and aiding environmental decision-making.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Potomac Conservancy, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (initially questioned being singled out, but generally complied with reporting).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires water utilities to report the monthly water consumption of data centers, making this information publicly accessible. This legislation aims to provide greater transparency on data centers' environmental impact, especially concerning water resources, and was supported by environmental groups and Senator Kannan Srinivasan.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new large data centers, including sound profiles and potential impacts on local resources, empowering localities to make more informed siting decisions.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Localities, community advocates, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul, Del. McAuliff, Senator Danica A. Roem.
opponents: Not explicitly stated in the provided snippets, but generally, data center developers might oppose stricter regulations that increase costs or limit development flexibility.
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law: Siting and Noise Studies
news_summary: HB 153, now law, requires localities to mandate site assessments for new data centers exceeding 100 megawatts, including sound profiles for nearby residential areas and schools. It also allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, providing tools for more responsible data center development, though it does not set specific noise limits or water caps.
